title: Clay Jones's big bass drum and cymbal
summary: Trumpeters helped young drummers; Happy describes Clay Jones's very large bass drum played with a cymbal in the other hand.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Mm-hmm . drums when you were playing if you made a mistake? You know I think Octave told me the trumpet player sometimes would kind of straighten him out when he was young.
Yeah, they did. They could kind of straighten him by seeing other drummers play. I played with John. I played with John McCollum.
What about Clay Jones? Did you ever hear him?
Bass drum? Yeah. He used to play with Clay Jones. He had a great big bass drum. One of them big ones.
That looks tall. That looks 36 inches or something. Wasn't that big, huh? Well, that's about as high as that. About as high as that pure old.
He used to do that thing all day and play it.
How would you guess that is? I don't know. Thirty inches? Thirty-two? Something like that, his drum?

Yeah, drum was somewhere around there. Yeah, that's a big one. Uh-huh. Oh, and they didn't use the cymbal beater. You know, like I got my cymbal beater. My cymbal beater. But he had another cymbal. This hand. That's how he used to play. Oh, yeah.
And he beat his bass drum at the same time with the other hand, huh? Left hand on the cymbal. Two cymbals together and then the right hand on the bass drum. That's it.
That's it. Well, the cymbal was that to be. Uh-huh.
